result.summary: Our patch adopts the correct defense-of-record for CWE-094: it verifies the resolved class is assignable to the expected base type (Property / FlippingStrategy) BEFORE any reflective construction, via a centralized MappingUtil.loadClass() helper. At the sinks it touches (PropertiesParser property+flipstrategy, XmlParser property+flipstrategy, PropertyFactory.createProperty, MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy, ConsoleOperations.createFeature) it is semantically equivalent to — and cleaner than — the official fix, closing the whole attack class, not just the observed payload. However, it misses two sibling sinks that the official fix patched: both YamlParser sinks (parseProperties + parseFlipStrategy) and ConsoleOperations.updateFlippingStrategy, leaving YAML-config-driven and console-update code injection reachable. Mechanism is sound; coverage is incomplete.
result.root_cause: Attacker-controlled class names from config files / HTTP params are passed to Class.forName(...).newInstance()/getConstructor(...).newInstance() with no type check, so any class with a matching constructor is instantiated (arbitrary code execution during construction).

dimensions.rationale: At every patched sink the type is validated before construction, closing the whole class there (not just the payload); but YAML and console-update sinks remain reachable.
dimensions.evidence: MappingUtil.loadClass() checks expectedType.isAssignableFrom(clazz) before asSubclass; used in PropertiesParser.parseProperties/parseFeatures, XmlParser, PropertyFactory.createProperty. YamlParser untouched.
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Fix is at the sink/trust boundary — the class is rejected before its constructor runs, exactly the reflective-injection root cause.
dimensions.evidence: loadClass throws IllegalArgumentException before clazz.asSubclass/newInstance; test NotAPropertyClass.INSTANTIATED proves constructor never runs.
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

issues.description: ff4j-config-yaml/YamlParser (parseProperties property sink and parseFlipStrategy) is not patched. The official fix guards both. YAML-config-driven code injection (Class.forName(...).newInstance() on attacker-controlled type/class) remains fully exploitable — a same-class sibling sink.

ConsoleOperations.updateFlippingStrategy still calls Class.forName(strategy).newInstance() without a type check; our patch only fixed createFeature. Official fix guards both methods, so the web console update path remains vulnerable.
Execution evidence is weak: pov_before_reproduced=false and regressions_ran=0/regressions_passed=null, so no-regression and POV-closure claims are not empirically confirmed by the pipeline.
